notes: v659 - the 'under $0.50 per $100' message now tells you what that means in YOUR money. It was a rate, and leaving you to convert it was why it did not land. $0.50 per $100 is simply 0.5% of whatever you invest, so the app now says it as a dollar figure on the position size you actually trade, worked out from your own position cap and account value: for example 'but it only earns $15 on a $5,000 buy - that is 0.30%, and brokerage plus the spread cost more than that'. That is the whole point of the test: on a $5,000 buy the brokerage alone is $6 and the spread on a cheap share can be $100 or more, so an edge of $15 is real in the statistics and worth less than the cost of collecting it. If the app cannot read your account it uses a $5,000 example and says so, rather than showing a figure based on nothing. Remember it is an AVERAGE over many trades, not a forecast for one. Display only; no scores or rules changed. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5).
